summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — defines data-collection standards for unfounded cases  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — requires tracking and reporting of unsubstantiated outcomes

North Carolina - Chapter 7B, Article 3 (Juvenile Code – abuse, neglect, dependency procedures)

regulations_applicable.title: Title 28 - JUVENILE JUSTICE AND DELINQUENCY PREVENTION (TRANSFERRED TO TITLE 14B)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of North Carolina
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals reversed adjudications of neglect and dependency and remanded because the trial court recited allegations rather than making its own findings linking the mother's conduct to the statutory definitions.
key_cases.relevance: Recited allegations unsupported by independent findings require reversal of the adjudication.
key_cases.quote: The fact that the child has special needs does not automatically render the child dependent or neglected.

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that verification of a juvenile petition under N.C.G.S. § 7B-403(a) is a jurisdictional prerequisite, so an unverified petition leaves the district court without subject matter jurisdiction and every order entered in the case is void ab initio.
key_cases.relevance: An unverified petition requires dismissal because the court never acquired power to act.
key_cases.quote: the district court could not exercise subject matter jurisdiction here in the absence of the verification

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed a termination order, holding that the trial court's findings did not support the conclusions of neglect or willful abandonment because the evidence failed to show a willful determination to forego all parental duties.
key_cases.relevance: Where the petitioner cannot meet the clear, cogent, and convincing standard, the petition fails and the case must be dismissed or reversed.
key_cases.quote: At the adjudication stage, the party petitioning for the termination must show by clear, cogent, and convincing evidence that grounds authorizing the termination of parental rights exist.

key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court vacated a termination order and remanded for new findings, holding that the trial court's findings of fact were insufficient to support termination on either neglect or willful abandonment, while rejecting the father's separate contention that the trial court's questioning of witnesses showed bias.
key_cases.relevance: It is recent NC Supreme Court authority that a petition fails and the order must be vacated where the court's findings, as opposed to recitations of testimony, do not establish the alleged grounds.
key_cases.quote: the trial court's findings of fact are insufficient to support its determination that respondent-father's parental rights in Nancy were subject to termination on the grounds of neglect and abandonment

Santosky v. Kramer standard not met
